analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. Changed head ranges: 404-413 (load/eviction memory release before eviction, outside the supplied units) and 1053-1073 (segmented paged KV parking). I examined both supplied units (lines 799-1646), which contain only the second hunk.

The new text describes parked free 64 MiB KV segments kept per pool, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. They are reinstalled for the next admission of the same size class. They are zero-fill-on-demand host-page wrapped. They are dropped on refused admission, on a process-wide release request, and after 30 s idle. There are env kill switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0.

Security-relevant observations for the integration pass:
- Parked KV segments are reused across requests (and thus across consumers) on the same provider. The doc says new segments come zero-filled, but the text does not say whether a reinstalled parked segment is zeroed or overwritten before reuse. That bears on T-028, residual GPU/KV data across requests, and A-001. A reinstalled segment is also not a new prefix-cache reuse path, since every KV row is written before it is read. I cannot verify the source (PagedKVSegments.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) from this doc diff, so I record this as an unverified implementation contract, not a finding.
- Parked bytes are outside the ledger charge. This is an availability/accounting question (T-029 and memory-pressure DoS), mitigated by the stated cap, idle drop and release on pressure. Also not verifiable here.
- The T-041 prefix-cache behavior is unchanged; the doc states media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture.
- Nothing in the diff changes the coordinator wire contract, attestation, keys or authorization.

No concrete regression is supported by the doc. The implementing code should be reviewed to confirm that reused parked segments are not readable stale across requests, and that the uncharged parked memory is bounded.
